title: Verbatim VBR520YP10SV2 Blu-Ray Disc BD-R XL 100GB 10 Pack $51.72 +Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Verbatim VBR520YP10SV2 Blu-Ray Disc BD-R XL 100GB 10 Pack $51.72 +Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU

[TheDukeOfNukem] I'd love if the recent PS5 mod scene managed to make BDRW work as a SSD alternative lol
[netsurfer] I'd love this deal to happen again:
Samsung 990 PRO 1TB M.2 SSD $55.92 Delivered @ Amazon UK via AU
[MrZ] I wish I had a BD-RW drive, I could really use some cheap storage.
[schquid] These aren't cheap per TB, even the current cooked HDD pricing still comes in better than BluRay. Also they're a pretty niche backup option, with dubious longevity if the dye breakdown issue is more than an urban myth.
[Odin] They don't use dye, they use metal ablative layer (MABL)
[Abaddon] Different media entirely. It's cheap storage if you aren't keeping discs spinning (and no need for refreshing written data on unpowered hard disks every few years)
[Knightchampion] Anyone able to recommend a cheap blueray burner for these?
[CheapGit] I've got a Verbatim 43888 unit which has a pioneer drive in it.
I paid just over $100 but they've seemed to have increased in price a lot.
Maybe have a look on the MakeMKV forum there is a few people sell flashed units on there.
[netsurfer] There doesn't appear to be one at the moment.
Pioneer BDR-UD03D 1.0 used to be ~$39. You need to wait and hopefully one of them gets discounted to that price range.
[GreenLego] I got one from AliExpress:
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005008980791700.html
It was $55 when I bought it last Nov, as with everything else, it has gone up in price. It shows as being able to do BD-R XL in ImgBurn, although I've only ever used 25gb BDs.
I see this one for less than $60:
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005006860826450.html
with coupons and cashbacks, you may be able to get it even cheaper. Comments say it can burn BD-Rs.
[kaboom mel] keen to know what is the use case for these with such high $/GB
[Wiadro] That gets boring after the first viewing
[Disabled-User] @adrianhughes1998:
Pron
There's a typo here, but judging by the replies it's clear that we are taking about the movie Tron.
[adrianhughes1998] @Disabled-User: Tron and Pron.
There's no typo - it's exactly what it jokingly refers to.
[tenpercent] @adrianhughes1998:
Watch with friends.
I'll be there for you
[Wiadro] @adrianhughes1998: Will they help with me with the story line?
[adrianhughes1998] @Wiadro: Of course they will.
They got your back (big clue there as to what transpires).
[Kommodore] Just another form of backup. People complaining about quality going down, but good quality blu-rays can last in storage for decades.
SSDs lose charge over time and go bad, hard drives mechanically fail, cloud storage has lost data before.
[Abaddon] Hard drives will also lose data over tine if not refreshed.
[Its4me] How does one refresh data on hard drives over tine? I have one that might benefit from this process.
[Odin] 100+ year lifespan
Better way to backup than SSDs or HDDs to be honest
[cobknob] Blu Rays are susceptible to disc rot but also any scratches your fu#$ed. For any archival values given with any media specifying life span, your assuming 2 big things:
The storage medium is kept in a temperature and humidity controlled environment free of dust and other harmful materials.
The media isn't defective - so always keep 2 backups of the same data from 2 different media batches.
[xmagic] Seems to be OOS now. Amazon UK listing at $198.
Just that using BDXL for backup seems to be not at a sweet spot for someone with about 1-2TB of data to backup on rotation. BDXL despite already much faster than other optical media, is still very slow.
Maybe it's time to seriously consider used LTO5 or LTO6 now.
[hawktalk] Those hold their value, but then again the 50gb version was a similar price at Dick Smith in the late 2000s / early 2010s
